description: I'm a multidisciplinary software engineer. Personally interested in EO, sustainability, conservation, and using tech for good. Open to anyone sharing similar interests
summary: An interactive 3D globe for exploring satellite imagery and environmental data. It opens focused study areas, mainly around Cape Town and the Western Cape, plus several global examples.
details:
Provide environmental scientists with supplemental decision-making software. Similar to Google Earth, but with layers for clouds, fires, soil moisture, SAR radar imagery, satellite markers, and risk colours. Estimating risk for flooding or fire. A NASA data panel explains the colour calculation with worked examples

Also showing NISAR satellite animation.

Use of X Grok, Claude, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Antigravity/AI Studio. Hosting by Grok, Streamlit Cloud, and onrender.com.

The globe is a React 19 and TypeScript app, built with Vite and styled with Tailwind CSS. Cesium draws the 3D Earth through Resium. Recharts draws the soil and rain charts. Framer Motion animates the panels. Kokoro.js speaks the briefing.

The API is Python with FastAPI and Uvicorn. httpx calls NASA and Anthropic. NumPy, pandas, xarray, h5py, rasterio, GeoPandas, and Shapely read the grids and the NISAR files. SQLite stores saved study sites. A companion page uses Streamlit, Folium, and Plotly. Tests use pytest.
